# Capability map

Headlines only: each `Cn` is a capability, with the count of Requirements that specify it. Requirement bodies are not rendered here — read them with krill's `get_feature_slice` / `get_requirement_slice` MCP tools, or re-render with detail.

## Telemetry pipeline

- **C1** — A board owner's board runs unattended for months, publishing readings that land in the database whenever the board and the broker can reach each other. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C2** — An operator can push a whole-board config that names, enables, disables, and sets the poll interval of that board's sensors without reflashing it. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C3** — An operator can query a reading alongside the sensor, board, and the location that sensor was in at the moment the reading was recorded. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Sign-in and ownership

- **C5** — A user can sign in to LeafLab and stay signed in across sessions, using the auth library already shared in the monorepo. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C15** — A user can edit, move, rename, and reconfigure the boards, sensors, locations, and plants they own, and cannot change anyone else's; everything is readable by every signed-in user. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C22** — An operator can scope reads so a user sees only their own boards, sensors, plants, and readings. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C23** — An admin can grant and revoke a LeafLab role for another user from the UI. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C24** — A signed-in user can claim an unowned board and become its owner. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C25** — An owner can release a board they own so the next person to hold it can claim it. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Boards and sensors

- **C4** — An operator can rename a sensor without breaking the continuity of that sensor's reading history. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C6** — A user can see every board and whether each one is currently reporting. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C7** — A user can open a board and see its sensors with each sensor's latest reading. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C8** — A user can see one sensor's readings over a time range they choose. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C9** — A user can rename a board or a sensor from the UI without losing its reading history. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C14** — A tinkerer can add a sensor to an existing board and have it show up in the UI without reflashing. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C18** — A tinkerer can lay out a board's sensors visually to match how the hardware is physically wired. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C19** — A tinkerer can rewire a sensor to different hardware and keep that sensor's reading history continuous, with the hardware change recorded. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C21** — A user can record and update the location a board physically sits in, as bookkeeping that never drives a reading's attribution. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Locations and placement

- **C10** — A user can create, rename, and nest the locations that describe their space, and see roll-ups reflect where things were at the time rather than where they are now. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C11** — A user can place a sensor in a location and move it later, and every reading stays attributed to the location that sensor was in when the reading was recorded. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Plants

- **C12** — A user can record a plant with a type and a location, as an entity distinct from the location it sits in. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C13** — A user can move a plant between locations and still see which readings were taken where that plant was living at the time. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Board provisioning

- **C16** — A board owner can flip a physical switch to put a board into provisioning mode and tell which mode it's in from the onboard LED. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
- **C17** — A board owner can enter Wi-Fi credentials and connection secrets on a page the board itself serves, without ever flashing firmware. (0 FR, 0 NFR)

## Alerting

- **C20** — A board owner can be notified when a sensor's reading crosses a threshold they set. (0 FR, 0 NFR)
